newsitem.title: USA: California settles with calcium manufacturers.
newsitem.headline: California settles with calcium manufacturers.

text.p: California said it reached settlements on Monday with eight leading manufacturers of calcium supplements and antacids for alleged violations of a state law requiring warnings on products containing lead.

California Attorney General Dan Lungren said the agreements settled lawsuits alleging the companies violated California's Proposition 65, which requires consumer warnings when toxic chemical exposure exceeds safety standards. Lead has been linked to brain damage and birth defects.

"Proposition 65 was passed by the voters to protect the public from known toxins such as lead," Lungren said. "I am pleased that these manufacturers recognize the importance of reducing lead levels in calcium supplements."
Lungren's office said the companies plan to reduce the amount of lead in their products but gave no other details of the settlements.
The non-profit environmental group Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) said Lungren's settlements did not go far enough to reduce lead levels.
"It's too much lead for too much time," NRDC attorney Al Meyerhoff said in a statement.

The settlements were reached with: SmithKline Beecham Consumer Healthcare, a unit of SmithKline Beecham Plc.; Warner-Lambert Co.; American Home Products Corp.; Pharmavite Corp.; General Nutrition Corp.; Perrigo Co. ; Schering-Plough Health Care Products Inc.; and Twin Laboratories.
